candidate_relations.reason: Lymphangioma circumscriptum usually produces grouped translucent vesicles, whereas examination finds a single deep, firm 5-cm labial mass.
No bluish discoloration, compressibility, or bleeding is described after inflammation subsides; the lesion remains firm and solid.
A vulvar fibroma can be firm and slow-growing, but clinical examination alone cannot supply the epithelioid smooth-muscle identity required by the reference.
Lipoma would generally be soft and mobile rather than the firm painful labial mass documented here.
The six-month indolent course, lack of nodes, and reduction of acute inflammation do not establish a malignant vulvar sarcoma.
No nerve-related symptoms or neurofibromatosis features accompany the solitary left labial lesion.
Re-examination specifically finds the swelling firm rather than cystic and without eversion of the labia minora expected from a Bartholin mass.
Vulvar tumor correctly recognizes the persistent solid labial neoplasm but does not identify its epithelioid smooth-muscle subtype.
A dermoid cyst should be cystic on palpation, unlike this firm solid mass after inflammatory signs resolve.
The lesion lacks soft compressibility or cutaneous lymphatic vesicles and instead presents as a circumscribed solid swelling.
An intact hymen and sexual naivety do not imply a Müllerian anomaly, and the abnormality is an acquired focal labial mass.
The firm consistency and recent severe pain are not characteristic of a vulvar lipoma, and no fatty imaging is provided.
Pain and inflammation improve within 24 hours, revealing a persistent noncystic 5-cm mass without fever or discharge.
Aggressive angiomyxoma is usually a soft, gelatinous, infiltrative pelvic-perineal mass, not established by this firm localized lesion.
The examination identifies a discrete 5-by-5-cm swelling rather than generalized enlargement of the labia.
No skin-surface nodule or adnexal features distinguish hidradenoma in the clinically described deep labial mass.
The examiner explicitly records that the residual swelling is not cystic.
There is no trauma or bruising, and a hematoma would not usually enlarge slowly for six months as a firm tumor.
Neither a cystic feel nor congenital inclusion features are present to support a vulvar dermoid.
The focal acquired labia-majora mass has no reported uterine, vaginal, or renal malformation suggesting a Müllerian duct anomaly.

case_quality_flags: No excision, histology, or immunohistochemistry is provided, so an epithelioid leiomyoma cannot be distinguished from other solid vulvar mesenchymal tumors from this record alone.
